requirements.evidence: All contract classes are present with the required signatures: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:17), UpdateQueue with nullable named params (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:15-21), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:21-26), QueuePermission with the single case Call (app/Enums/QueuePermission.php:7), QueueAccess model with the array cast and both relations, a factory that keeps membership and queue in the same entity, and QueuePolicy with create/update/manageAccess/call. The call order is right on both paths: CallNextTicket authorizes after the inactive check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32), and Ticket::call locks the queue, then checks inactive, then authorizes, then raises the waiting LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:98-115). Revoke is only logged when `$deleted > 0` (SetQueueAccess.php:60). The migration has the FKs with cascade and the unique key. Weak spot: the DB-race-to-ValidationException conversion relies on string sniffing (`'23000'`, 'UNIQUE', 'Duplicate', CreateQueue.php:63-67). A PostgreSQL unique violation (23505, "duplicate key") would not match and would surface as a raw QueryException, and on MySQL any 23000 integrity error is mislabeled as a slug duplicate.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through app/Actions with authorization inside each action (`Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize(...)`). The policy is the single source of truth. The migration has a generated timestamp name (2026_10_29_045945_...) and a reversible down(). The model is mass-assignment safe via `#[Fillable([...])]`, which matches the sibling Ticket model. business-rules.md, database-schema.md and the CHANGELOG 'Added' section are all updated. Minor gaps: no PHPDoc on the new public `__invoke` methods of CreateQueue and UpdateQueue, while SetQueueAccess has one.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes before any write. The policy denies non-members, members of other entities and employees without a grant, and treats corrupted values as deny (`is_array(...) && array_is_list(...)`, QueuePolicy.php:504-507). A grant row forged for a member of another entity is denied because the lookup goes through `membershipFor($queue->entity_id)`. SetQueueAccess rejects non-string or unknown permissions with a strict in_array, and rejects a cross-entity membership/queue pair before writing. Ticket::call now enforces the per-queue grant instead of plain entity membership. No weaknesses found.

tests.evidence: There are thorough Pest tests: CreateQueueTest, UpdateQueueTest, SetQueueAccessTest (audit expectations including 'no revoke log' and invalid-permission datasets), QueuePolicyTest (corrupted grants, forged cross-entity row) and QueueCallAuthorizationTest (every call mode, ordering of inactive/auth/logic errors). The existing CallNextTicketTest was adapted to use a manager caller (`pfCallNextManagerFor`) without weakening its assertions. Gap: in UpdateQueueTest 'rejects an empty name and converts a database race to validation', a queue with slug 'corrida' already exists, so ensureSlugIsAvailable throws before the updating hook ever runs. The UpdateQueue DB-race path is therefore not actually exercised.

simplicity.evidence: ensureSlugIsAvailable and rethrowUniqueViolation are copy-pasted between CreateQueue.php:48-76 and UpdateQueue.php:67-97. The hand-rolled unique-violation detection could be replaced by catching Laravel's built-in `Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException` (available in this Laravel version, which supports the `#[Fillable]` attribute). QueueAccessFactory runs about 80 lines of afterMaking/entityFor logic for the same-entity requirement, which is heavier than needed. Otherwise the code is direct: QueuePolicy is small, and the CallNextTicket change is one line.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are small, and the style matches siblings. There is a helpful comment on the lock order in Ticket::call (Ticket.php:89-91). No dead code or debug output. Small nits: the double read of the ticket in Ticket::call (once unlocked to get queue_id, once locked) needs its comment to make sense, and the factory's entityFor branching takes some effort to follow.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: the actions, enum, model, policy, factory, migration, the Ticket/CallNextTicket authorization changes, the required docs/CHANGELOG updates and tests. There is no UI, no delete action and no unrelated refactor. The edits to CallNextTicketTest were needed because the new authorization would otherwise break those tests.

issues.explanation: Unique-violation detection sniffs SQLSTATE '23000' and the uppercase strings 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate': a PostgreSQL 23505 'duplicate key' error would escape as a raw QueryException, and any MySQL integrity error (FK, NOT NULL) would be misreported as a slug duplicate. Catching UniqueConstraintViolationException would be both correct and simpler.

The 'database race' test creates the conflicting 'corrida' queue up front, so the pre-check throws ValidationException before the updating hook runs and the QueryException conversion in UpdateQueue is never exercised.
ensureSlugIsAvailable and rethrowUniqueViolation are duplicated almost verbatim across the two actions.
The afterMaking/entityFor logic is heavier than needed to keep membership and queue in the same entity, and it creates DB rows even on make().
The new public __invoke methods lack PHPDoc, which the docs-sync convention asks for on touched public methods (SetQueueAccess has one).

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue, UpdateQueue and SetQueueAccess actions, a queue_access table/model/factory/enum, and a QueuePolicy that is enforced on both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call in the required order, with docs, CHANGELOG and thorough tests. Authorization and validation are solid and scope is tight. The main weaknesses are fragile, duplicated unique-violation sniffing that would not convert PostgreSQL duplicates, and a race test for UpdateQueue that never reaches the code it claims to cover. Approvable with minor follow-ups.
